title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Officers of the Company
tiers.description: Directors, officers and employees of the Company. Subject to the full Policy: general principles (6.1), the 12-month short-term trading guidance (6.2), the prior-notification and confirmation procedure (6.3, 6.5), and Blackout Periods (6.4) subject to the exceptional-circumstances consent process (6.6).

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Subset of Officers of the Company; distinguished for the Blackout Period exceptional-circumstances consent route (Chairman consultation instead of full Board) and for statutory notification of changes in relevant interests and in contracts conferring a right to call for or deliver Company shares, within 14 days (s205G Corporations Act) or 5 business days (Listing Rule 3.19A.2) to ASX via the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Representatives of the Service Providers
tiers.description: Directors, officers and employees of the Company's external Service Providers (e.g. Magellan Asset Management Limited, which provides research and trade execution). They abide by their own employer's Trading Policy rather than this Policy's clearance/blackout procedures, but remain subject to the Corporations Act insider trading prohibition described in section 4.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Respective associates of Officers of the Company, including a company or trust controlled by them, a spouse, dependant children, a close relative, or a person acting in concert with them.

windows.end_anchor: end of the Trading Day of the Company's announcement of its interim financial results
end of the Trading Day of the Company's announcement of its final financial results

windows.start_anchor: close of business on the last Trading Day of each month
windows.end_anchor: end of the Trading Day of the Monthly Net Tangible Asset per Share announcement

rules.detail: 'Company Securities' is limited to shares, debentures (including convertible notes), units and options to acquire or subscribe for shares issued by the Company; 'deal' is defined only as subscribing for, purchasing or selling Company Securities or agreeing to do so. A third-party OTC put/call written by a bank over the shares is not itself a 'Company Security' and its creation is not expressly a 'deal', so entry into the derivative overlay is not clearly caught by the Policy's clearance/blackout regime (though a resulting sale or transfer of the underlying shares would be).

Independently of the Policy's clearance procedure, a Director must notify ASX (via the Company Secretary) within 5 business days of any change in interests in a contract that confers a right to call for or deliver Company shares - language that squarely covers an OTC put/call collar.
rules.evidence: a director of the Company must notify ASX within 5 business days after any change in ... interests in contracts to which the director is a party or under which the director is entitled to a benefit, and that confer a right to call for or deliver shares in or debentures of the Company

rules.detail: No hedging or 'limiting economic risk' provision appears anywhere in the Policy.
Monetisation is not named. An agreement to sell Company Securities (e.g. a prepaid forward) is a 'deal' under section 4, triggering the section 6.1(c)/6.5 prior-approval and notification process.
rules.evidence: to 'deal' in Company Securities includes subscribing for, purchasing or selling Company Securities or entering into an agreement to do any of those things.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not named and, like other third-party derivatives, are not 'Company Securities'.

Broker credit and non-standard settlement are prohibited, but the prohibition is expressly stated not to extend to normal documented margin lending or loan facilities from banks or other lending institutions offered to the general public. No separate clearance step is stated for entering such a facility.
rules.evidence: Such prohibition does not extend to normal documented margin lending or loan facilities offered to the general public by brokers, banks or other lending institutions.

rules.detail: Encumbrance is not named, but is a necessary incident of the expressly-permitted margin lending/loan facility carve-out (such facilities are secured on the shares).
rules.evidence: Such prohibition does not extend to normal documented margin lending or loan facilities offered to the general public by brokers, banks or other lending institutions.

rules.detail: The carve-out extends to 'loan facilities' generally, not just margin loans, from 'brokers, banks or other lending institutions'. It is qualified to facilities 'offered to the general public', which is arguably a poor fit for a bespoke bilateral loan negotiated privately to secure a single executive's collar.
rules.evidence: Such prohibition does not extend to normal documented margin lending or loan facilities offered to the general public by brokers, banks or other lending institutions.

rules.detail: Directive (though phrased as 'should never') against short-term trading, defined as purchase with a view to resale, or sale with a view to repurchase, within 12 months. Carve-out for sale of shares immediately after conversion of a security (e.g. option exercise).
rules.evidence: Generally speaking, Officers of the Company should never engage in short term trading of Company Securities. In general, the purchase of Company Securities with a view to resale within a 12 month period and the sale of Company Securities with a view to repurchase within a 12 month period would be considered to be transactions of a "short term" nature.

financing_disclosure: Directors: any change in a relevant interest in Company Securities, to ASIC/ASX (via the Company Secretary), within 14 days (Corporations Act s205G); any change in interests in contracts conferring a right to call for or deliver Company shares (which includes an OTC option/collar), to ASX (via the Company Secretary), within 5 business days (Listing Rule 3.19A.2).

external_documents: Trading Policies of the Service Providers (e.g. Magellan Asset Management Limited), which govern Representatives of the Service Providers in place of this Policy's clearance/blackout procedures
exemption_authority: The Company Secretary, after consultation with the Board (or the Chairman, if the applicant is a Director), may in their discretion consent to dealing during a Blackout Period, but 'will generally refuse' unless exceptional circumstances (such as financial hardship or a court order) exist.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Securities... includes any shares in the Company, debentures (including convertible notes) issued by the Company, units of shares in the Company and options to acquire or subscribe for shares in the Company... to 'deal' in Company Securities includes subscribing for, purchasing or selling Company Securities or entering into an agreement to do any of those things.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A third-party OTC put/call collar is arguably neither a 'Company Security' nor itself a 'deal', so its creation may fall outside this Policy's clearance and Blackout Period regime entirely, though this interpretation carries risk and should be confirmed with the Company Secretary before relying on it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Director ASX disclosure of option-like contracts
bespoke_clauses.clause: a director of the Company must notify ASX within 5 business days after any change in ... interests in contracts to which the director is a party or under which the director is entitled to a benefit, and that confer a right to call for or deliver shares in or debentures of the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the internal clearance process does not reach the collar, a Director must still notify ASX (Appendix-3Y-style) within 5 business days of entering it, and must tell the Company Secretary promptly so that filing can be made.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending expressly excluded from broker-credit ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: not utilise broker credit ... Such prohibition does not extend to normal documented margin lending or loan facilities offered to the general public by brokers, banks or other lending institutions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is not banned outright, though the 'offered to the general public' qualifier creates doubt as to whether a bespoke bilateral facility for one executive squarely fits the carve-out.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the purchase of Company Securities with a view to resale within a 12 month period and the sale of Company Securities with a view to repurchase within a 12 month period would be considered to be transactions of a "short term" nature
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar's settlement disposes of shares within 12 months of their acquisition and any repurchase intention is present, it risks being characterised as prohibited short-term trading; a straightforward one-way exit is less likely to be caught.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A "Blackout Period" operates in respect of ... the close of business on 31 December and 30 June ... and ... the last Trading Day of each month up to the ... Monthly Net Tangible Asset per Share announcement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies granting the Board a general discretion to declare extra confidential blackouts, MFF's Blackout Periods are limited to fixed, predictable reporting dates, making collar timing more certain.

summary: A funded collar is plausibly achievable, and on unusually favourable terms if the narrow definitions are read literally. 'Company Securities' and 'deal' are defined narrowly (the Company's own shares/debentures/options, and subscribing, purchasing, selling or agreeing to do so), so the OTC put and call legs of a collar with a bank may not themselves be caught by the Policy's Company Secretary approval process or Blackout Periods at all, though this reading should be confirmed given the general principles in clause 6.1. The loan leg is expressly not banned: normal documented margin lending or loan facilities from banks or lending institutions are carved out of the broker-credit prohibition, though the 'offered to the general public' qualifier leaves some doubt for a bespoke bilateral facility. Directors must separately notify ASX within 5 business days of entering any contract conferring a right to call for or deliver Company shares, which squarely covers an option-based collar, and within 14 days of any change in relevant interest. Any actual sale or transfer of the underlying shares (e.g. on settlement) is a 'deal' requiring prior notification to, and subsequent written confirmation with, the Company Secretary, must avoid the fixed half-year and monthly NTA Blackout Periods (absent exceptional-circumstances consent), and should not be structured to look like short-term trading within 12 months of acquisition.
